title: Where it grows
subtitle: The Loire and South Africa
objectives: Explain its history in South Africa
Name other countries that grow it

steps.title: The Loire
steps.body: Chenin Blanc's home is the Loire's Anjou-Saumur and Touraine. Key appellations: Vouvray and Montlouis in Touraine; Savennières, Saumur, Anjou, Coteaux du Layon, Bonnezeaux and Quarts de Chaume in Anjou. Tuffeau, a soft limestone, and schist give different styles. It's been grown there since at least the 9th century.

steps.title: South Africa
steps.body: South Africa grows more Chenin than anywhere else, around 17,000 hectares, about 18% of its vineyards. Called Steen locally, it arrived with the first Dutch settlers in the 17th century. It was long used for brandy and bulk wine; now old bush vines in Swartland, Stellenbosch and Paarl make some of the country's finest whites.

steps.prompt: Match each place to its Chenin.
steps.explanation: Chenin shines in the Loire and South Africa.

steps.title: Elsewhere
steps.body: Chenin grows in California, once widely for bulk wine, Argentina, Australia, New Zealand and Mexico. A few cool-climate producers in the US and Australia now make serious dry Chenin. But the Loire and South Africa remain its two great homes.

steps.prompt: What is Chenin Blanc called in South Africa?
steps.explanation: Steen is the traditional South African name.

steps.title: What you learned
points: The Loire's Anjou and Touraine are Chenin's home
South Africa grows the most, as Steen
Old bush vines make South Africa's finest Chenin
